title: v3 Phase 2: graph decomposition + governed flows + onboarding overhaul + routed-review wiring
summary: Four streams, one release. R-0003: decompose the dependency graph into component nodes (hybrid directory-convention + import/reference cohesion, AST symbol clustering for oversized files, components.yaml override, granularity floor) stored as a layer in graph.json, each carrying a fingerprint-cached lens map computed by the shipped R-0001 detector engine; reviews assemble the capped union of touched components' maps with a structural fail-open that only ever WIDENS. R-0004: execute/evaluate/fix each compile to ONE journaled Claude Dynamic Workflow run per stage between human gates (one workflow file per stage following the review-wave.js pattern), emitted from tp.py behind the SAME workflow_available() gate, with the MANDATORY byte-identical Task-dispatch fallback as the reference implementation and the only Codex path. R-0005: README install decision tree by account type (org members cannot install from GitHub — say so), per-host quickstarts, v3 feature docs, tp onboard truth-up, all pinned by named CI/test checks. R-0006: evaluate consumes routed briefs (em full-catalog mandate + audit cadence untouched), fixtures-path discount in detector scoring (D-0002), routed-audit hybrid measured and decided against a >=30%-reduction/zero-escape bar (D-0003), audit machinery extracted from loop.py into taskplane/audit.py byte-frozen (D-0004).
decision: Adopt the composite approach A: component layer inside graph.json derived by a new taskplane/decompose.py (hybrid heuristics, floor: module decomposes at >=8 files or a >=600-line file; a cluster earns a node at >=2 files or >=4 top-level symbols spanning >=120 lines; residual <module>::core), consumed by route v2 as a cached-map union re-evidenced on the live diff with floors applied after assembly and a traced fail-open to the module route; three stage workflow files consuming verbatim dispatch prompts with schema-pinned receipts, emitted by tp.py (loop.py/lens.py/audit.py stay workflow-agnostic, test-pinned) behind workflow_available(); README restructured around an account-type install decision tree with CI grep/docs-drift/row-count/link checks and onboard context fixtures; evaluate wired to stage='build' routing with the R-0001 budget inherited verbatim, fixture-path discount at x0.25 for fixture-only signal support with goldens regenerated only via regen.py, the routed-audit hybrid decision recorded against a measured bar (default decline), and the loop.py audit machinery moved to taskplane/audit.py under a byte-frozen differential replay.

current_state.summary: Phase 1 (v2.4.0) shipped route v2 and the review wave: lens.route() gates the signal path on stage + catalog stage_profiles and fails open to legacy breadth=all (taskplane/lens.py:196-233); _route_v2 restricts candidates to the stage profile, keeps floored lenses, and refuses unevidenced n/a (taskplane/lens.py:336-451); dispatch_briefs emits contract:lens-brief with ADDITIVE verdict/score/evidence fields plus the routing_decision object (taskplane/lens.py:587-699). The detector engine is a SPECS table + generic scorer (taskplane/lens_signals.py:219-512, 540-616) with budget cap 8 demote-never-drop and post-budget security/architecture floors (lens_signals.py:741-784); fixture paths are NOT discounted, so fixture-only diffs inflate i18n/mobile (D-0002, lens_signals.py:537 context). The graph has directory-level modules only (depgraph.module_of, taskplane/depgraph.py:222-256), an incremental mtime+hash scan under a file lock (depgraph.py:486-755), and a content_fingerprint stamped over code-file hashes + edges (depgraph.py:168-201); there is NO component layer and no lens data on nodes. The loop wires lenses per step: evaluate/em route the real diff with breadth '"all" if step == "em" else "routed"' and NO stage argument, so evaluate still runs the LEGACY route (taskplane/loop.py:841-856); the em audit machinery (cadence, router_audit, gate auto-filing, _audit_brief) lives inline in loop.py:1426-1680 (D-0004) and the em gate enforces full-catalog coverage, evidence-backed n/a, and router-regression blocking (loop.py:1692-1804). Workflow capability detection is tp.workflow_available (conservative: Codex always unavailable, kill-switch 0/false/no/off, opt-in, default unavailable; taskplane/tp.py:891-931); tp lens dispatch emits workflow-or-task with the task path stdout byte-identical and the choice traced as review_dispatch_path (tp.py:1034-1062); workflows/review-wave.js is the only workflow (pure-literal meta, FINDINGS_SCHEMA pinned to contract:findings-v2, deterministic; workflows/review-wave.js:18-81); TestNoWorkflowOnlyGate pins loop.py/lens.py workflow-agnostic and the em breadth literal (taskplane/tests/test_review_wave.py:346-361); parity goldens regenerate ONLY via taskplane/tests/fixtures/briefs/regen.py (env/path scrub, sorted keys). Execute waves run via loop.wave/claim into .tp-work/<task> worktrees with per-task slots; workers submit and never advance (loop.py:431-548, 1807-1858). The dashboard renders v2 coverage and the review graph (taskplane/dashboard.py:1146-1263, 1293-1330); depgraph.to_html draws modules only (depgraph.py:1328-1370). README documents only individual-account install flows (README.md 'Install' section) and tp onboard prints a context-blind checklist (tp.py:96-, 1605-1620). Debt: D-0002 (fixture inflation), D-0003 (audit sweep cost), D-0004 (loop.py accretion) are recorded addressed-by-R-0006. Codex has no workflow runtime (verified, docs/v3-strategy-flows-lenses-onboarding.md addendum). Baseline graph fingerprint 10bcb08711d396c2bb69529e89c10670e0645da2dbe0419292471fc0d8cefa9c; scanned_head 20422079 predates HEAD 16795c96 by version-stamp/docs-only commits (no code files), so a refresh scan is content-fingerprint-stable.

alternatives.name: Selected composite: hybrid decomposition layer + per-stage workflow files + README decision tree + wire/discount/measure/extract
alternatives.description: R-0003: components derived by directory convention + import/reference cohesion with AST symbol clustering for files >=600 lines, floor-gated, stored as a graph.json layer with fingerprint-cached lens maps computed by the shipped R-0001 engine; route v2 consumes the capped union of touched components' maps with floors on the live diff and a structural fail-open to the module route. R-0004: one workflow FILE per stage (execute/evaluate/fix-wave.js) on the review-wave.js pattern, ONE run per stage between human gates, emitted from tp.py behind workflow_available(); Task dispatch stays the byte-identical reference. R-0005: one README with an account-type install decision tree, per-host quickstarts, v3 feature docs, tp onboard truth-up, all pinned by named CI/test checks. R-0006: evaluate wired to stage='build' routing (R-0001 budget inherited verbatim), fixtures-path discount x0.25, routed-audit hybrid measured against a >=30%/zero-escape bar with the decision recorded (default decline), audit machinery extracted to taskplane/audit.py byte-frozen.

gains: Component precision where this repo actually hurts (one directory, three files over 2,000 lines) — symbol clustering is the only derivation that can decompose dashboard.py, the pinned acceptance case

Every new behavior is additive and gated (components key absent = byte-identical routing; workflows unavailable = byte-identical dispatch; discount regenerates goldens via the documented path), so rollback is data/flag removal, not migration
Resumable stage waves remove the measured v2.3.0 credit-cutoff redo cost while the reference dispatch path stays the definition of correctness
The debt trio (D-0002/3/4) is burned down inside the same release that builds on the affected code, with byte-frozen proofs where behavior must not move
costs: Symbol-level clustering adds an AST pass and a component index to maintain (bounded: floor caps component count at O(tens); fingerprint cache makes rescans no-ops)
Three new workflow files plus extended goldens grow the parity-maintenance surface (bounded: goldens regenerate only via regen.py and CI owns the diff)
The audit extraction differential corpus must be captured BEFORE the move — a sequencing constraint on the plan
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Component attribution proves noisy in dogfood (attribution disagreeing with reviewer judgment on >1 review per release), the stage-wave journal shows resume defects the dispatch path does not have, or the audit-hybrid measurement beats the bar and a follow-up requirement supersedes the audit shape

alternatives.name: R-0003 alternative: pure import-graph clustering (community detection)
alternatives.description: Derive components solely by clustering the file-level import graph (modularity/community detection), no directory or symbol heuristics.

gains: No convention assumptions; works identically across languages the scanner covers
No components.yaml needed for well-modularized repos
costs: Cannot decompose a single large file at all — imports are file-level, so taskplane/dashboard.py stays one node and the pinned >=3-components acceptance criterion is unreachable on this repo

Cluster boundaries are unstable under small edits (community detection is globally sensitive), which churns fingerprints, defeats the lens-map cache, and makes per-component attribution drift between scans
Not explainable: a reviewer cannot see WHY two files share a component, weakening the honesty story the coverage map depends on
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The repo grows many multi-file feature directories where import cohesion outperforms convention, AND a stability constraint (fixed seeds/anchored clusters) makes fingerprints reproducible

alternatives.name: R-0003 alternative: path-prefix heuristics only
alternatives.description: Components = second-level path prefixes under each module (pure convention, no cohesion or symbol analysis).

gains: Trivially deterministic, near-zero cost, easy to explain
No AST dependency for non-Python files
costs: Blind to cohesion and to file size: taskplane/ (one flat directory of 15 files) stays ONE component forever — exactly the under-decomposition R-0003 exists to fix
Encourages component sprawl on deeply nested repos (every directory a node) unless a floor is bolted on anyway
No basis for distinct per-component dependency sets when files in one directory serve different features
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Never as the sole mechanism; it survives INSIDE approach A as the first-pass grouping that cohesion then refines

alternatives.name: R-0004 alternative: one generic parameterized stage-wave.js
alternatives.description: A single workflows/stage-wave.js taking {stage, briefs} via args and selecting phases/schemas at runtime.

gains: One file to maintain instead of three
New stage types need no new workflow file
costs: The shipped test pattern pins each workflow's meta as a PURE static literal and its schema as a static constant checked WITHOUT a JS runtime (test_review_wave.py static scans); runtime schema/phase selection weakens exactly those determinism pins
Execute/fix agents return submission receipts while evaluate agents return findings-v2 — a generic schema must union them, loosening per-stage output validation
A defect in the shared file breaks all three stages at once; per-stage files fail independently
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The Phase 3 flow executor makes stages fully data-defined AND the workflow runtime grows schema-per-agent selection that static tests can still pin

alternatives.name: R-0004 alternative: status quo (Task dispatch only, no stage workflows)
alternatives.description: Keep execute/evaluate/fix on today's Task-based dispatch exclusively; ship no new workflow files.

gains: Zero new parity surface; nothing to detect or fall back from
No dependency on host workflow runtime behavior or org policy
costs: Every mid-stage death stays a full redo — the v2.3.0 credit cutoff re-ran four lens agents from scratch with no journal; the same class of loss recurs on every long execute wave
Leaves the shipped R-0002 capability detection and the platform's one-workflow-per-stage guidance unused beyond review
R-0004's acceptance criteria are unimplementable — this alternative is the fallback RAIL, not the release
tradeoffs.revisit_when: This IS the permanent fallback and the reference implementation; it remains selected automatically wherever workflows are absent, disabled, or killed

alternatives.name: R-0005 alternative: split per-audience install docs behind a thin README
alternatives.description: Move install instructions to docs/install-<audience>.md files; README links out.

gains: Shorter README; per-audience pages can go deeper
Docs-drift checks scope naturally per file
costs: The observed launch failure happened ON the README at GitHub — org members never reached a working path; adding a hop relocates the dead end instead of removing it
Marketplace/launch snippets quote the README; split pages multiply the surfaces the forbidden-claim grep must police
Two sources of install truth drift against each other
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The README's install section outgrows one screen per audience even after the decision tree, or a hosted docs site becomes the canonical landing page

alternatives.name: R-0006 alternative: adopt the routed-audit hybrid immediately; leave audit code in loop.py
alternatives.description: Switch the em audit to routed-deep + verification-sweep now (saving tokens immediately) and defer the loop.py extraction again.

gains: Immediate audit token savings without a measurement phase
costs: Weakens the ONE backstop that polices every other narrowing decision in this phase before any measurement exists — the audit must be the last thing allowed to get cheaper, and only with proof (zero escaped n/a-lens findings)
Deferring the extraction again compounds D-0004 exactly when this phase ADDS evaluate wiring to loop.py (3,191 lines), and re-blocks the Phase 3 precondition the strategy names
An unmeasured adoption cannot be recorded as an evidence-backed decision, so D-0003 stays open in spirit
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The measured comparison beats the bar (>=30% token reduction, zero escapes) — then adoption arrives as a follow-up requirement with the measurement attached, which is precisely what this design ships instead

contracts.description: NEW. The component layer stored under the top-level `components` key in graph.json, written only by `graph scan --decompose` (taskplane/decompose.py via depgraph.scan) and read by route v2 and the dashboard graph view. Shape: components[{id, module, files, symbols, fingerprint, deps, lens_map}] where id is `<module>::<cluster>` (never colliding with module ids or boundary prefixes), files/symbols are the span, fingerprint is sha256 over the sorted (file, hash, symbol-span) material, deps are component-level edges [{to, kind}], and lens_map is {lens_id: {verdict, score, evidence}} computed by lens_signals.route_verdicts over the component file set and recomputed ONLY on fingerprint change. Overridable via components.yaml. Absent key = layer absent = module-level routing byte-identical; the modules/edges sections are never touched by decomposition.

ADDITIVE change to the dispatch-brief payload emitted by lens.dispatch_briefs (id, name, tier, agent, model_tier, task_slot, output, read-only contract spec, verbatim prompt, verdict, score, evidence): briefs and the routing_decision gain component_attribution — {lens_id: [component ids]} naming which component contributed each routed lens — and the same payload family now also feeds the evaluate stage (stage='build' routing) and the stage-wave workflows. No existing key changes meaning or shape; the Codex Task-dispatch stdout for an undecomposed workspace stays byte-identical (parity goldens).

NEW. One-run-per-stage compilation for the governed stages between human gates. The tp.py stage emitter (behind workflow_available(), kill-switch 0/false/no/off always forces dispatch) wraps the UNMODIFIED stage dispatch payload as workflow{name, args} where name is execute-wave|evaluate-wave|fix-wave and args IS the same brief set the Task path prints; agent() outputs are schema-pinned per stage — execute/fix: receipts[{task, outcome, note}]; evaluate: the contract:findings-v2 shape — with retry-on-mismatch. Runs are journaled and resumable (completed agents return cached results); no generated run contains an approval/gate step; the Task-dispatch fallback is MANDATORY, byte-identical on stdout, and the only path on Codex.

Schema-pinned findings.json shape per lens/evaluate agent: lens id + findings[{severity, class, file, line, title, scenario, fix}] plus meta.lens_coverage carrying the full routing decision {lens: {verdict, score, evidence|negative_evidence}} — UNCHANGED in this phase. Consumers move but the shape does not: the audit machinery that reads it (router_audit, _router_audit_gate, decision extraction) relocates to taskplane/audit.py under the byte-frozen differential, the evaluate wave's workflow agents are schema-pinned to it, and findings meta additionally carries component_attribution (additive, via contract:lens-brief).

rollout.strategy: Additive and gated per stream, shipped as one release. R-0003: land decompose.py + the components layer behind the explicit `graph scan --decompose` flag (no flag = no layer = byte-identical routing, existing suites prove it); dogfood the first decomposition on this repo and review the derived components before relying on component-routed reviews; component assembly engages only when the layer is present and current. R-0004: land the three stage workflows + the tp.py emitter behind workflow_available() (default conservative: dispatch), enable via TASKPLANE_WORKFLOWS=1 on the dogfood host first; the dispatch rail remains the default and the reference everywhere. R-0006: land the evaluate wiring and the discount together with the regen'd goldens as one reviewed diff; capture the audit differential corpus BEFORE the extraction commit, then move the code; run the D-0003 measurement during this phase's own em review and record the decision. R-0005: install-truth README changes land first (separable, unblocked); feature docs land with the features they document; CI legs (grep, docs-drift extension, row-count) land with the docs.
rollout.rollback: Per stream, no data migration anywhere. R-0003: stop passing --decompose and/or delete the components key from graph.json (modules/edges untouched by construction) — routing reverts to Phase 1 behavior immediately; components.yaml removal reverts overrides. R-0004: TASKPLANE_WORKFLOWS=0 (org/operator kill-switch) instantly pins every stage to the dispatch rail, which is CI-guarded byte-identical throughout; deleting the stage workflow files has the same effect. R-0006: revert the discount commit and re-run regen.py to restore prior goldens; revert the extraction commit (pure move; loop.py re-exports mean no caller churn in either direction); the D-0003 decision is a registry record, not a behavior change. R-0005: docs revert freely; CI legs are independent jobs that can be disabled without touching the test suite.

lens_evidence.evidence: Approach coherence: one mechanism family carries all four streams — the shipped R-0001 detector engine computes the per-component maps (R-0003), the shipped R-0002 emitter/capability pattern carries the stage waves (R-0004), the shipped audit machinery relocates without behavior change (R-0006), and the docs state exactly what those mechanisms do (R-0005); nothing invents a second routing model, a second scheduler, or a second install truth. Dependency boundaries: four named contracts isolate the component layer (component-map), the brief handoff (lens-brief, additive-only), the stage compilation (wave-workflow, wrap-not-rewrite), and the findings shape (findings-v2, unchanged); all proposed modules are existing depgraph nodes; depth bounded contract-only. Trade-offs: seven real alternatives across the streams, each with gains/costs/revisit_when, including two status-quo options kept as permanent fallback rails rather than strawmen. Failure modes: seven concrete modes with detection+recovery, every one failing toward more coverage or the reference rail. Verifiable delivery: all 7 anchored R-0003 criteria map 1:1 with named test files, and all 20 R-0004/R-0005/R-0006 criteria are mapped in secondary_requirements; the guardrail statement enumerates eleven enforcement surfaces with a strict-or-stricter argument each, and the two structural invariants (superset fail-open, byte-frozen extraction) are proven by construction plus pinned tests, not by intention. Self-attested: I am the designer; no independent lens agent ran against this contract — surfaced at the approval gate per policy.
